items.label: 3M Q2 FY2026 (07-21-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Q2 2026 call detail (CFO Anurag Maheshwari): Safety & Indust

set.signal: Q2 2026 call detail (CFO Anurag Maheshwari): Safety & Industrial delivered 8.2% organic sales growth, with double-digit growth across electrical markets, industrial adhesives and tapes, abrasives and industrial specialties; safety grew high single digits and roofing granules returned to growth; first-half Safety & Industrial growth was 5.7%. Transportation & Electronics grew 5.9% in Q2 (first half 2.9%) on the expected backlog conversion. Consumer was down 2.1% for the quarter and 1.7% for the half: U.S. point-of-sale growth was positive in 18 of the 26 weeks year to date, but tightening of inventory levels at several key retailers in the second half of June more than offset it (CEO Bill Brown: about a one-week delta, expected to normalize, with Consumer flat to up slightly in the back half). Growth in all five regions: China grew double digits (CEO: first half about 8%; the China business is 50/50 domestic production and export, with more than 5,000 people and six factories), U.S. and Canada industrial grew mid-single digits, Europe returned to growth up mid-single digits, and Asia grew double digits led by India for seven straight quarters. CEO Bill Brown: price was 1.6% in Q2. Operating profit included $110 million of tariff impact and stranded cost headwind, and 3M has not received any tariff refunds to date. GAAP EPS was $1.78, growing 33%.

items.reason: Attribution: the Q2 price figure was stated by the CEO, not the CFO named in the entry header.
items.evidence: Bill Brown: Look, it's a great question, Chris. Q2, our price was at 1.6%, so it was about in line with what we'd expected.

items.label: 3M Q2 FY2026 (07-21-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Capacity and operations (CEO Bill Brown): utilization, measu

set.signal: Capacity and operations (CEO Bill Brown): utilization, measured across about 300 assets covering more than half of volume, is running around 63.5%, 64%, leaving plenty of upside capacity in aggregate, but some assets are constrained and short of demand - notably the New Ulm facility, which produces cable accessories and electrical connectors for electrical markets facing high and increasing demand ('That volume is spiking'). A multi-week sprint there achieved record production levels in June, delivering $13 million of incremental revenue (nearly 50 basis points at the Safety & Industrial level); over time there might be some capital there. Cost of poor quality improved 60 basis points and overall equipment effectiveness 140 basis points year-over-year; CFO Anurag Maheshwari: inventory improved seven days year-over-year. Utilization data across the 100 plants in the network underpins a three-to-five-year transformation to consolidate assets, cells and factories.

items.reason: Attribution: the seven-day inventory improvement was stated by the CFO, not the CEO named in the entry header.
items.evidence: Anurag Maheshwari: ... Our inventory's improved by seven days year-over-year

items.label: Texas Instruments Q2 FY2026 (07-22-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Demand outlook (CEO Haviv Ilan): 'we see a setup of a strong

set.signal: Demand outlook (CEO Haviv Ilan): 'we see a setup of a stronger demand; it's broader' - the above-seasonal Q3 guide draws on all markets. Automotive demand built up through the quarter, led by China and by EVs and hybrids (he believes the cost of fuel drove that), and automotive customers had taken inventory to very low levels: 'I think we are in the start of a cycle that is very broad.' Industrial is still maybe five or six points below its 2022 peak against a mid- to high single-digit trend-line growth; energy infrastructure and test and measurement were the fastest-growing sectors in the first half, the data center is providing a tailwind into industrial, and customers 'have not yet built inventory'. CEO: personal electronics is expected to grow sequentially in Q3 but at a lower level than its typical Q3 growth (sometimes mid-teens), as shortages are putting pressure on customers. IR head Mike Beckman: aerospace and defense, energy infrastructure and robotics grew at higher rates, every sector and region grew, and he attributes it more to secular content growth than pricing; backlog built throughout Q2, both in orders for immediate shipment and in backlog further out. CEO: TI picked some market share last year, and competitors quoting lead times 52 weeks away are an opportunity as customers sometimes start new designs.

items.reason: Attribution: the personal-electronics outlook was the CEO's, but it sat after the IR head's statement and read as his; backlog comment (IR head) now attributed.
items.evidence: Haviv Ilan: ... I expect this business to be growing sequentially, but maybe at a lower level. ... Mike Beckman: ... we did see backlog build throughout the quarter

items.label: Texas Instruments Q2 FY2026 (07-22-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Capacity and loadings: incoming CFO Julie Knecht said factor

set.signal: Capacity and loadings: incoming CFO Julie Knecht said factory loadings increased from Q1 to Q2 and continued to increase throughout Q2; Q3 loadings depend on demand, with clean room space available to equip. CEO Haviv Ilan: TI is equipping Richardson RFAB2 at a very high level, has a full clean room 'available almost in Sherman 1' plus a second shell in Sherman 2; Lehi 2 - needed as embedded growth picks up after Lehi 1 absorbed the transfer of Stellaris manufacturing from foundries - will have its shell at the end of this year, with no new customer qualifications needed. 'In general, we are good for the next three years' on clean rooms (phase three: modulate the equipment). CFO Rafael Lizardi: inventory ended Q2 at $4.6 billion, down $90 million from the prior quarter, at 196 days (down 13 days sequentially).

items.reason: Attribution: the inventory figures were stated by the CFO, but followed CEO statements unattributed.
items.evidence: Rafael Lizardi: Inventory at the end of the quarter was $4.6 billion, down $90 million from the prior quarter. Days were 196, down 13 days sequentially.

items.signal_prefix: Outlook detail from the call, beyond the Q3 revenue ($5.65 b

set.signal: Outlook detail from the call, beyond the Q3 revenue and EPS ranges already on the release entry: Q3 effective tax rate about 13%; operating expenses, net other income and expense and acquisition charges flat from Q2 (CFO Rafael Lizardi); fall-through of 70%-85% excluding depreciation is a good placeholder (Julie Knecht), with gross margin 'a little higher' rather than flat (Lizardi). 2026 capex 'continues to be $2 billion-$3 billion' - 'If anything, it could be on the higher end of that midpoint, just given demand'; future capex will be disproportionately in assembly test operations outside the U.S., which do not get the investment tax credit, while TI continues to get 35% ITC on U.S. front-end manufacturing, which can be choppy. Capital intensity rule of thumb stays 1.2x the growth; 2027 capex numbers will come at the capital management call in February. CEO Haviv Ilan: the free cash flow framework is still valid - $8 billion-$9 billion at $20 billion of revenue and $9 billion-$10 billion at $22 billion.

items.label: Shell Q2 FY2026 (07-30-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Q2 2026 results (CFO Sinead Gorman): adjusted earnings of $9

set.signal: Q2 2026 results (CFO Sinead Gorman): adjusted earnings of $9.8 billion and over $21 billion of cash flow from operations despite the ongoing disruptions in the Middle East; free cash flow of 'some $17 billion in one quarter'. LNG trading and optimization captured significant additional value versus the prior quarter. Chemicals made a positive free cash flow contribution and the CFO called the quarter's chemicals results 'the best we have seen in over five years', weighted more toward cost take-out and asset operating performance than margins (the Monaca, Pennsylvania complex hit record performance). CEO Wael Sawan: refineries achieved a record 102% utilization, shifting output toward middle distillates such as jet fuel; Brazil delivered another quarter of record production. Net debt was reduced to some $42 billion, or $12 billion excluding leases.

items.reason: Attribution: the 102% refinery utilization and record Brazil production were stated by the CEO, not the CFO named in the entry header.
items.evidence: Wael Sawan: ... Our refineries achieved a record 102% utilization in a high-margin period.
